en.title: Norway: public petroleum wealth and the limits of domestic productive capacity
en.deck: Norway converts offshore resource income into foreign public savings, but parliamentary fiscal decisions, mainland productivity, welfare staffing, housing and power networks determine what the accumulated wealth can deliver.
en.regime: Petroleum-exporting welfare economy with a large externally invested public fund, parliamentary fiscal guidelines and deep European market integration, constrained by labour, housing and infrastructure capacity.
en.key_risk: Confusing globally invested fund assets with immediately available domestic productive capacity conceals workforce, housing, electricity-grid and resource-depletion constraints.

pt-BR.title: Noruega: riqueza pública petrolífera e limites da capacidade produtiva doméstica
pt-BR.deck: A Noruega transforma renda offshore em poupança pública externa, mas decisões fiscais parlamentares, produtividade continental, pessoal dos serviços, moradia e redes elétricas determinam os resultados do patrimônio acumulado.
pt-BR.regime: Economia de bem-estar exportadora de petróleo, com grande fundo público investido externamente, diretriz fiscal parlamentar e integração europeia profunda, limitada por capacidade de trabalho, moradia e infraestrutura.
pt-BR.key_risk: Confundir ativos globais do fundo com capacidade produtiva doméstica imediatamente disponível oculta limites de pessoal, moradia, redes elétricas e esgotamento de recursos.

selection_rationale: The published NBIM/GPFG study explains delegated portfolio ownership but not Norway's domestic fiscal, productive and social transmission mechanisms. A broad country context connects its parliamentary budget, offshore revenues, mainland industry, EEA and European gas dependence, labour-intensive welfare state, housing, ageing and electricity networks, adding reusable context to sovereign wealth-flow and European security research.
contrary_evidence: The country's large public financial assets and renewable power base counter a simple fiscal-fragility interpretation, while labour, housing and grid constraints remain material.
The fund strengthens fiscal resilience but does not directly finance domestic productive capacity; its returns also expose wealth to global markets.
European gas demand supports export earnings, but resource depletion, demand shifts and regulation limit long-run permanence.
Population continues growing through births and migration, yet ageing increases care-sector demand and qualification and housing constraints slow labour adjustment.
limitations: 2027 budget amounts are proposals subject to parliamentary approval, not realised spending.
2026 mainland GDP figures are forecasts from different vintages.
GPFG allocation is a 30 June 2026 portfolio snapshot, not domestic investment.
Electricity production refers to 2025 and varies with hydrology.
Demographic projections depend on fertility, mortality and migration assumptions.
EU gas-import shares do not measure all European energy use.
Sámi rights and land-use issues require case-specific evidence and attribution.
